statedReasoning: Per the fully-fetched bill text and důvodová zpráva (submitted 8 Dec 2025 by Richterová, Bartoš, Ančincová, Pipášová, Martínková Španihelová, Šmída, Volpe), the bill's stated aim is 'snížení nákladovosti systému doplňkového penzijního spoření' (lowering the cost structure of supplementary pension savings) via three narrow numeric changes to zákon č. 427/2011 Sb.: (1) §60 odst. 3 — removes the differentiated management-fee ceiling so ALL účastnické fondy (participant funds), not just the mandatory conservative fund, are capped at the conservative-fund rate; combined with (2) the DZ's stated intent, the effective ceiling for ordinary participant funds drops from up to 1% p.a. to 0.4% p.a.; (3) §60 odst. 4 similarly unifies the performance-fee ceiling, cutting the ordinary-fund cap from up to 15% to 10% of positive returns; (4) §192 odst. 3 písm. a) — cuts the transformed-fund (pre-2013 legacy) management-fee coefficient from 0.8 to 0.4, matching MPSV's own comment requesting fee symmetry across all fund types. The DZ argues Czech pension-fund fees are high relative to international comparators (cites Revolut ~0.12% p.a., Swedish public conservative funds 0.08–0.22%) and that some funds charge the statutory maximum even with negative returns. Stated effect: higher net returns for savers, stronger incentive for savers to rely on returns rather than state contributions alone, and competitive pressure on pension companies. Explicitly stated: NO fiscal impact on the state budget or other public budgets — this is a pure private-market fee regulation. Effective date proposed: 1 July 2026.
researchedContext: Legislative history (psp.cz) confirms the bill was distributed as print 71/0 on 16 Dec 2025, sent to government for comment 18 Dec 2025, and received a NEUTRAL government position (not opposition) distributed as print 71/1 on 13 Jan 2026. The Organizational Committee recommended proceeding 14 Jan 2026, assigning rapporteur Ing. Libor Turek, Ph.D. and the Rozpočtový výbor (Budget Committee, RV) as guarantor. As of 24 July 2026 — over six months later — the bill remains at this same pre-first-reading stage; no reading has occurred despite the neutral government stance and zero fiscal cost, which would ordinarily be a low-friction path to passage. This is a legislative-process observation (stalled despite a neutral government signal), not itself evidence of any conflict. Substantively, 427/2011 Sb. governs the doplňkové penzijní spoření (post-2013 third-pillar product); the amended provisions (§60, §192) govern fee ceilings charged BY pension companies (penzijní společnosti) TO savers — the bill's direction runs AGAINST industry fee revenue and FOR consumers, the opposite direction from what a self-dealing hypothesis would predict for sponsors with any pension-industry tie.

unstatedEffects.effect: The fee cuts (management fee 1%→0.4% for ordinary participant funds, performance fee 15%→10%, transformed-fund coefficient 0.8→0.4) directly reduce revenue for the regulated pension-management industry (penzijní společnosti) as a sector, even though the DZ frames the measure only in terms of saver benefit; no pension company or asset manager is named, and the DZ presents no industry consultation or impact estimate on pension-company margins.
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: Third-pillar savers gain higher net returns; pension-management companies as a sector lose fee revenue — a sector-wide, not company-specific, effect with no named winner or loser entity.

conflictAssessment: No plausible self-dealing channel, and the bill's substantive direction (cutting fees pension companies may charge) runs opposite to what a sponsor-benefits-an-industry-tie hypothesis would predict. None of the seven sponsors holds a recorded money tie to a pension company, asset manager, or third-pillar product provider: Ivan Bartoš and Hana Ančincová carry only the graph's generic zero-value 'OSVČ' (company:ico:04627695) self-employment marker, which recurs identically across many sponsors in this batch and batch-001 with a flat 0 CZK figure and no distinguishing detail — a data-quality artifact, not a substantive tie. Lenka Martínková Španihelová's tie to MATURUS, o.p.s. (1,197,779 CZK) is, per independent verification, a graphic-design social enterprise employing people with disabilities, founded by the Jedlička Institute Foundation, that she directed before entering Parliament — a nonprofit (o.p.s. legal form, which cannot legally be a 'penzijní společnost, a.s.' under 427/2011) wholly unrelated to pension-fund fee structures. Olga Richterová, Barbora Pipášová, Martin Šmída, and Samuel Volpe carry no recorded money ties at all. Symmetric with batch-001's finding: this is universal consumer-protection regulation with no channel to any sponsor-linked entity, and here the direction (fee reduction) is affirmatively anti-industry, reinforcing the absence of a conflict.

citations.claim: Tisk 71 amends 427/2011 §60 odst. 3 and 4 (unifying and lowering the management-fee ceiling from up to 1% to 0.4% p.a., and the performance-fee ceiling from up to 15% to 10%, for ordinary participant funds to match the mandatory conservative fund's existing rate) and §192 odst. 3 písm. a) (cutting the transformed-fund management-fee coefficient from 0.8 to 0.4), citing international fee comparators (Revolut ~0.12%, Swedish public conservative funds 0.08–0.22%) and stating no fiscal impact on public budgets. Effective 1 July 2026. Signed by Richterová, Bartoš, Ančincová, Pipášová, Martínková Španihelová, Šmída, Volpe, Prague 9 Dec 2025.

Legislative history: distributed as print 71/0 on 16 Dec 2025, government issued a NEUTRAL position (print 71/1, 13 Jan 2026), Organizational Committee recommended proceeding 14 Jan 2026 with rapporteur Libor Turek and the Budget Committee (RV) as guarantor; no first reading recorded as of 24 July 2026.
The amended supplementary-pension-savings statute is zákon č. 427/2011 Sb., o doplňkovém penzijním spoření — a real, in-force Czech law.

Sponsor Lenka Martínková Španihelová's recorded money tie, MATURUS, o.p.s. (~1.2M CZK), is a nonprofit graphic-design social enterprise employing people with disabilities (Jedlička Institute Foundation), not a pension company or financial-product provider.
Sponsors Ivan Bartoš and Hana Ančincová hold only the generic, zero-value graph 'OSVČ' self-employment marker, recorded at 0 CZK with no company-specific detail.
